title: Why I Built Postmello
deck: Friendship deserves room to grow, before and beyond a first phone.
description: A request to borrow a phone became a place for independent friendships, creative letters and time away from the screen.

title: A World Built for Childhood
deck: A complete world for imagination, independence and real friendship.
description: A desk to explore, a world to make their own, and real friends to create for. The design choices that make Postmello a place built for children.

figure.alt: The Postmello desk with a painted mountain letter, a mailbox, paper and named friend drawers.
figure.caption: The desk is the interface. Every friend has a drawer; every letter has a place.

title: Three Kinds of Quiet
deck: Time to make something. Time to answer. Time away.
description: How sound, the postal ritual and the absence of presence signals protect the space around a letter.

figure.alt: A blank moon-and-stars writing page with drawing tools along its edge.
figure.caption: The page has room for whatever the letter becomes.

title: A Letter Keeps Its Audience
deck: Writing back respects the people a letter was meant for.
description: Why Postmello has no forwarding action, and why a reply goes to the sender or the original group.

title: The Name on the Desk
deck: Room for expression, with a familiar name underneath.
description: Nicknames, hero icons and the names we give our friends make the desk personal while keeping its writer recognizable.

title: What the Bee Knows
deck: A small courier makes the waiting understandable.
description: How the mailbox, waking bee and connection notes tell the truth about a letter’s journey.

figure.alt: The courier bee asleep inside the hanging hive.
figure.caption: The resting courier is part of the desk’s explanation of waiting mail.

title: Learning the Desk Through Its Objects
description: Paper, drawers, envelopes and a mailbox give correspondence a place and each touch a consequence.

title: A Friend Does Not Need Another App
deck: The correspondence continues across devices and inboxes.
description: Email in both directions, shared addresses and careful merging keep letters and friendships together.

figure.alt: An example email message and the same words set on a Postmello letter.
figure.caption: Words from an inbox arrive at the desk on paper. Example correspondence.

title: A Space of Your Own
deck: How a practical edge became a place with a view.
description: The evolution from one desk to personal spaces, with familiar objects and room for imagination.

figure.alt: The Baan Na desk background with ricefields beyond the wooden back rail.
figure.caption: Baan Na background art: the writing surface has a view beyond its edge.
